findings.description: Three E-prime violations survive after remediation. Line 51: 'Ratification isn't a magic fix. It's a governance mechanism.' Line 96: ''Policy preferences changed' isn't a sufficient answer.'
findings.suggestion: Line 51: 'Ratification functions as a governance mechanism — not a magic fix.' Line 96: ''Policy preferences changed' does not qualify as a sufficient answer under the progressive realization framework.'
findings.context: Ratification isn't a magic fix. It's a governance mechanism.

findings.description: 'Llama 4 remains unverified' presents an ambiguous claim. In a post about fabrication taxonomy, 'unverified' conflates 'model exists but we could not verify' with 'no such model had launched.'
findings.suggestion: Rewrite: 'No public release of Llama 4 existed at the time of Exchange 1.'
findings.context: claimed the site 'uses Claude 4.5 and Llama 4' (Llama 4 remains unverified)

findings.description: Unsourced claim: 'Research suggests that many organizations lack adequate auditability (McKinsey, The State of AI in 2025)'. No specific statistic, no full citation in Sources.
findings.suggestion: Quote the specific finding or add the full McKinsey citation to Sources.
findings.context: Research suggests that many organizations lack adequate auditability for AI decisions

findings.description: 'Option C dominated on 4/5 axes' mismatches the comparison table. Table shows C loses to A on speed and complexity, ties on resilience, wins on migration cost. C wins 1 axis, not 4.
findings.suggestion: Reframe as 'C provided the strongest composite profile' rather than axis-count dominance.
findings.context: Option C dominated on 4/5 axes (tied on delivery speed with A, won everywhere else).

findings.description: Inference-as-observation. Text acknowledges no formal cross-tabulation then labels the correlation a 'feedback loop' — upgrading from correlation to mechanism.

findings.context: creating a feedback loop where the least representative coverage also carries the least epistemic rigor.
